questions.q: What is a Tier 1 analyst primarily responsible for?
options: Only running vulnerability scans on a fixed schedule
Writing all of the SOC's correlation rules from scratch
Approving the organization's annual security budget
Monitoring the alert queue, doing initial investigation, and escalating alerts that exceed their access or certainty
questions.explain: Tier 1 is the first set of eyes on the queue — triage, basic investigation, and escalation when needed.

questions.q: What separates Tier 2 from Tier 1 in this lesson's model?
options: There is no real difference between the two tiers
Tier 2 has broader access and tooling to investigate deeper and actually perform incident response
Tier 2 never looks at alerts that Tier 1 has already seen
Tier 2 only works night shifts while Tier 1 only works days
questions.explain: Tier 2 takes Tier 1's escalations, confirms them with deeper access, and performs real containment and response.

questions.q: What does a Tier 3 analyst do that Tier 1 and Tier 2 generally don't?
options: Handles the very first alert that appears in the queue each morning
Proactively threat hunts and tunes the correlation rules and detection tooling based on what they find
Exclusively handles password reset tickets
Is the only tier allowed to read any logs at all
questions.explain: Tier 3 doesn't wait for alerts — they hunt for what rules miss, and they own tuning the rules themselves.

questions.q: In the failed-login-then-success example, why does Tier 1 escalate to Tier 2 instead of closing the alert?
options: The successful login came from an unusual country right after the failures, exceeding Tier 1's access and certainty
Escalation happens automatically for every single alert regardless of content
Tier 1 analysts are never allowed to close any alert
The alert had no useful information in it at all
questions.explain: An unusual-location success right after failed attempts is exactly the kind of uncertainty that calls for Tier 2's deeper access.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what is a typical real-world career progression into this field?
options: There is no typical progression — tiers are assigned randomly
Student directly into Tier 3 with no Tier 1 or Tier 2 experience
Student, then Tier 1 for roughly one to two years building judgment, then Tier 2, then Tier 3 or a specialized role
Tier 3 first, then Tier 2, then Tier 1 last
questions.explain: The usual path builds investigation judgment at Tier 1 first, before taking on Tier 2's deeper response work and beyond.
